title: The quartet with Marian
summary: Back in Chicago they form a quartet, Marian moving toward more modern harmony.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We got back to Chicago there and we took off a little time and we finally, Marian and I, Marian says, I want to play, I want to play. I said, okay, let's go. So I booked a job and at that time I was still mean inside. I mean I was still from that War deal you know. And I was drinking a little too much too. Let's
be honest about it. I mean, I must be honest about it.

And she said, let's rehearse. I said, oh no, well get on the job and rehearse then. Let them pay us for our rehearsals. (LAUGHTER). We don't need to rehearse, you know, we're..... So we did, we were very good we did have a rehearsal. Just one rehearsal. Went on the job with the quartet and started going. And Marian was playing my style. Swing, I call it swing. It's some dixieland numbers, but not many dixie. It was mostly swing and you know, get in the groove and swing.

So we were doing quite well but Marian with her great harmonic sense of music and harmonies and everything, she leaned towards Oscar Peterson and people. You know, that's, that style. Which was good, it was more modern and harmonically very fine. George Shering and so we played around and came back to New York finally. She started to get real good when she was swinging.

Now she started to get that beat and the rhythm and she was playing up a storm. So I said, well, I thought to myself it's time to go to New York. So I booked a job in Philadelphia and then New York and she was playing real good and I got sick, I got the flu,
